title: Hosted API Demo: Chat & Text Generation Basics
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Lumen Finance through Hosted API chat/text generation basics: streaming, parameters, retries and idempotency, plus a short Console tour and cost/latency guidance. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a high-throughput customer-service assistant; security and data residency questions remain. Next step: run small benchmark, share security pack and pricing options.
transcript:
Header: 2026-05-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Samir Patel (Redwood); Aisha Khan, Tom Rivera, Priya Desai, Miguel Ortiz (Lumen Finance)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood inference, i'm the AE on your account, with Samir who's our solutions engineer. How are we doing today?
00:07 Aisha: Good thanks. Appreciate you setting this up. We wanted a demo of your hosted API for chat and some details on streaming and retries - trying to understand fit for our customer support assistant project.
00:15 Samir: Awesome. We'll start with a quick overview of the Hosted API then jump into a live demo of chat generation, show streaming, parameters like temperature/top_p/max_tokens, and talk about retries and idempotency patterns.
00:28 Tom: Quick context: we're currently prototyping with OpenAI but hitting cost and latency at scale. Also our infra runs in AWS eu-west-1 and we need SOC2 and KMS integration.
00:38 Jordan: Perfect, that's the right context. Redwood's hosted tier supports SOC 2 compliance and customer KMS integrations via our Private options, but for hosted we provide audit logs and customer controls - we'll share the security pack.
00:49 Samir: Jumping into the API. (screen share) Here's a simple chat call: POST /v1/chat/completions to the Redwood API with model parameter, messages, and streaming enabled. We'll run a quick example.
01:05 Samir: (typing) sending request now - you should see tokens stream back.
01:14 Speaker 1: okay yeah we're seeing the partials - looks smooth. Streams arrive as chunked events; you can use server-sent events or websockets depending on client.
01:25 Aisha: Is streaming real-time or buffered? We care about first-byte latency.
01:30 Samir: Good question. Streaming is near-real-time; first-byte latency depends on model size and sequence length. On our curated smaller chat models first-byte is typically 80-150ms in eu-west under hosted SLA; larger LLMs can be higher.
01:45 Tom: How do you handle interrupted streams or network retries? If a client drops halfway we can't duplicate messages to the user.
01:52 Samir: We recommend idempotency keys for request side - send an idempotency header and the server will dedupe. For resumed sessions we also expose token-level offsets in the stream so you can request continuation. We also provide guidance on backoff: exponential with jitter.
02:10 Priya: Are you doing automatic retries in SDKs? What about at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics?
02:17 Samir: Our official SDKs have configurable retry logic with idempotency support. By default we do safe retries for 5xx errors and timeouts; stateful streams require client-side resume logic. Exactly-once is hard for streaming; we push for idempotency keys and client-side reconciliation.
02:33 Jordan: From a procurement perspective, note that Dedicated nodes give you stronger latency guarantees and isolation, but hosted iterates faster and is lower friction to start.
02:41 Aisha: We're leaning hosted for POC to avoid infra ops. But we want to measure cost per session - we have 10k monthly active users with ~150 tokens per session.
02:50 Samir: For 150 tokens/session at that scale, our Optimize tooling suggests batching and prefix caching to cut token costs; we'll run numbers after the call.
03:02 Miguel: Can you demo parameter tuning, like temperature and top_p, to get more deterministic responses for policy-critical messages?
03:09 Samir: Yeah - here. (demo) Set temperature to 0.0 for deterministic, 0.2 for low variance, etc. Top_p at 0.9 retains diversity. Max_tokens caps output. Also show stop sequences and function-calling hooks for structured outputs.
03:28 Aisha: Are function calls supported on hosted? We need structured JSON outputs for downstream systems.
03:33 Samir: Yes, function/tool calling is supported on the hosted API. Example shown: define a schema, model returns JSON and we validate. Note: parsing errors can happen; we recommend schema validation and a retry-loop.
03:46 Tom: On the topic of cost/latency - how do we pick model family? We need <200ms median latency for short replies.
03:52 Samir: For <200ms median you'll look at smaller quantized variants; Redwood catalog has verified profiles per model + region. We can route low-latency traffic to optimized variants. If you need strict SLOs we can discuss Dedicated pools.
04:10 Aisha: About security: encryption at rest, KMS, and audit logs - Hosted can integrate with our SSO?
04:17 Jordan: Hosted supports SAML SSO for the Console; for keys, hosted stores keys in our KMS but we can discuss bring-your-own-key on Private or Dedicated with customer KMS. We'll send the security pack with SOC2 reports and network diagrams.
04:31 Priya: Data residency - do logs or prompts leave region? We need EU-only for some customers.
04:36 Jordan: Hosted supports regional data handling; for strict residency you can use Private deployment in your VPC or Dedicated in a region. We'll map the options in the security doc.
04:50 Samir: Back to demos - here's an example of a retry scenario. I force a 502 and show the SDK retry flow: it retries 3 times with exponential backoff, logs are surfaced to Console traces.
05:08 Miguel: What about costs for retries? If we get a flapping upstream and retries multiply tokens that's a risk.
05:15 Samir: Right - we recommend idempotency and server-side dedupe to avoid duplicate billing. On the SDK we can disable automatic retry on non-idempotent calls. Also Optimize can detect anomalous retry patterns.
05:30 Aisha: Any limits on streaming throughput? We expect spikes during product launches.
05:36 Jordan: Hosted has per-account rate limits but supports quota increases. For bursty production, Dedicated with autoscaling or hybrid routing is common.
05:46 Tom: Can we run a small benchmark? 100 concurrent sessions, 150 tokens each, eu-west region - measure p50/p95 and cost.
05:54 Jordan: Absolutely. Next step: we'll run a hosted benchmark and share results. We'll need an API key and sample prompts; Samir can coordinate.
06:02 Samir: I'll follow up with a benchmark plan. For the benchmark we'll collect p50/p95 latency, token counts, and error rates.
06:10 Aisha: What about observability? We need per-route latency and token-level cost breakdown.
06:15 Samir: Console gives per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, traces, and error analysis. We'll show a quick Console screenshot.
06:25 (short screen pause)
06:32 Tom: Licensing - if we scale to 1M sessions/month, what's the pricing model?
06:37 Jordan: Hosted usage-based per token with volume tiers; Dedicated is committed capacity. We'll send a pricing sheet tailored to your volumes.
06:45 Priya: Any compliance caveats for financial data?
06:48 Jordan: We'll include compliance notes; Private deployment is the strongest option for regulated financial data. Hosted can be acceptable depending on controls and redaction.
06:58 Aisha: Great. Any known limitations with your streaming for multi-turn chat where we keep long context + KV cache?
07:05 Samir: We support KV cache and prefix caching. For very long contexts we recommend chunking and retrieval-augmented pipelines. There can be tradeoffs in tokenization and memory; Optimize has recommendations per workload.
07:18 Miguel: Can you share a short example of retry headers and idempotency?
07:23 Samir: Sure - X-Idempotency-Key header example and a sample response that includes resume_token. I'll share sample snippets in the follow-up.
07:35 Jordan: Recap and next steps - run hosted benchmark, share security pack and pricing, Samir to send SDK snippets and idempotency examples, schedule follow-up in two weeks.
07:45 Aisha: That sounds good. Thanks everyone.
